content.user_title: Set Sales Quotas From Capacity and Territory Data
content.value_statement: Sales targets can exceed realistic capacity and distribute opportunity unfairly. This skill guides quota planning through ramp-adjusted capacity, territory allocation, and documented validation checks.
actual_capabilities: Calculate Ramped Rep Equivalents and estimate capacity using quota levels and historical average attainment.
Reconcile revenue commitments with capacity and explain options for handling shortfalls.
Evaluate over-assignment percentages against attainment history and compensation cost tolerance.
Allocate quotas using historical territory results, scored potential, or equal splits for shared opportunity pools.
Define ramp relief schedules, relieved-quota attainment rules, and mid-cycle change governance.
Review quota-to-OTE ratios, implied pipeline coverage, and attainment distributions with separate B2B and B2C calibration.
limitations: Provides planning guidance and formulas, not a packaged calculator or built-in CRM integration.
Requires reliable performance history, ramp assumptions, and territory data for defensible recommendations.
Included benchmark figures require independent verification and updates; B2B SaaS ratios should not be applied directly to B2C teams.
Does not design compensation plans, build full pipeline coverage models, or provide individual deal coaching.

use_cases.title: Reconcile an annual revenue commitment
use_cases.description: Compare the board target with ramp-adjusted team capacity before assigning quotas and selecting an over-assignment percentage.
use_cases.target_user: VP of Sales or Chief Revenue Officer

use_cases.title: Allocate quotas across unequal territories
use_cases.description: Use historical results or scored territory potential to distribute targets and document review rules.

use_cases.title: Set targets for a growing retail team
use_cases.description: Plan monthly unit targets and new-hire relief using internal sales history instead of B2B SaaS benchmarks.

prompt_templates.title: Begin a first quota plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set next quarter's quotas for [team size] sellers in [business type]. Ask one question at a time and identify required inputs before modeling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: collect context and choose an appropriate planning approach.

prompt_templates.title: Check capacity against a target
prompt_templates.prompt: Our target is [amount] for [period]. We have [headcount], with ramp factors [factors], full-period quota [amount], and historical average attainment [percent]. Calculate RREs, estimate capacity, and explain the gap before recommending allocation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: reconcile a committed target with realistic capacity.

prompt_templates.title: Compare territory allocation methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Allocate an approved aggregate quota of [amount] across territories with historical results [values] and potential scores [scores]. Compare history-based and potential-based shares, identify unreliable inputs, and propose governance for mid-cycle changes. Request approval before finalizing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: select an allocation method for unequal territories.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose and redesign a quota process
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our current plan using [rep-level results], [ramp schedule], [territory changes], [OTE], and [win rates]. Distinguish average attainment from the share of reps reaching quota. Compare capacity, allocation, and distribution scenarios within [deadline] and [analyst hours]. Verify benchmark dates and definitions, document assumptions, and obtain approval at each planning stage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: diagnose an existing plan and define a repeatable review process.

output_examples.input: Illustrative capacity check: 16 RREs, $800,000 annual quota per fully ramped rep, 50% average attainment, and an $8 million company target.
output: Reconciliation options: add capacity, revise the target, or explicitly accept the shortfall risk.
Approval checkpoint: confirm capacity assumptions before choosing over-assignment and allocating quotas.

output_examples.input: Illustrative allocation: distribute an approved $20 million aggregate quota across territory potentials of $15 million, $12 million, $10 million, $8 million, and $5 million.
output: Territory A: 30% share and $6 million quota.
Territory B: 24% share and $4.8 million quota.
Territory C: 20% share and $4 million quota.
Territory D: 16% share and $3.2 million quota.
Territory E: 10% share and $2 million quota.
Validation required: confirm potential scores, capacity, and the scoring model refresh date before final approval.

output_examples.input: Illustrative ramp exception: a $200,000 full-quarter quota, an approved 50% ramp factor for that quarter, and $80,000 achieved sales.
output: Attainment against relieved quota: $80,000 divided by $100,000 = 80%.
Apply the documented relief policy consistently and route territory reassignments through the formal approval process.

best_practices: Use period-aligned ramp factors and distinguish average attainment from the percentage of sellers reaching quota.
Verify benchmark dates and definitions across independent sources; use internal history to calibrate B2C plans.
Approve assumptions section by section and document territory scoring dates, relief rules, and change approvals.
anti_patterns: Divide a revenue commitment by nominal headcount without validating ramp-adjusted capacity.
Apply flat quotas to unequal territories or add a fixed cushion without examining attainment history.
Raise individual quotas to hide a capacity shortfall or change territory assignments without formal approval.

faq.question: What information should I prepare?
faq.answer: Provide the planning period, target, headcount, ramp positions, territory structure, and performance history. OTE and win rates support additional sanity checks.

faq.question: Can this skill support B2C teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It adapts capacity, allocation, and ramp relief to B2C while using internal history instead of transferring B2B SaaS benchmark ratios.

faq.question: Does it connect to our CRM automatically?
faq.answer: No built-in CRM connector is included. Supply authorized data through your existing workflow and verify its completeness before modeling.

faq.question: Are the benchmark figures automatically current?
faq.answer: No. The references contain dated figures, not a live data feed. Verify source dates, definitions, and applicability before relying on them.

faq.question: Will it design commission rates and accelerators?
faq.answer: No. It checks quota-related ratios and identifies compensation concerns, but directs compensation plan design to a separate skill.

faq.question: Does it retain our approved plan?
faq.answer: The instructions request retention of approved decisions when persistent memory is available. Actual retention depends on your assistant environment and memory settings.
